City Guides

# The Lisbon Guide

Published on:June 1, 2017

![Image 1](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/lisbon-guide-liam-mckay-VHWyqXsWHg0-unsplash.jpg)

Like all European cities, Lisbon oozes with history (truly, you can't turn a corner without running into a castle or a UNESCO World Heritage Site), but it's also been home to a meaningful renaissance as of late, with flocks of young creatives taking advantage of the city's inexpensive rent and high livability factor. The result is a celebration of Portugal's unique culture both in real time, and with respect to the countless monarchies and armies that ruled the city in centuries past, all in a locale that's a stone's throw from both seaside resorts and wineries that are considered some of Europe's best. The city itself is built on a series of hills that are most easily navigated by foot, and though that's all the better for burning off egg pastries and extra glasses of port, you'll also want to take advantage of trams (most famously the antique Tram 28) to assist with some of the more onerous steeps. The many elevations of the city also offer constant viewpoints, with photo-worthy vistas of the river from nearly every street and restaurant. Several locals helped us suss out the best spots, including actress Annabelle Wallis, who grew up in the nearby, and enviably adorable, town of Cascais.

Hotels

[![Image 2](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/independente-1.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/bairro-alto/the-independente-hotel [link_8])

[Independente Principe Real](link_8)

83 Rua Sao Pedro de Alcantara, Bairro Alto

Part hotel, part hostel, the Independente feels a little bit like Portugal's version of the Ace. While we wouldn't recommend the hostel rooms unless you're on a tight budget, the suites are lovely, with memorable design quirks like vintage colored leather chairs, bedside lamps made from plumping pipes, and the coolest tile floors in the bathrooms. Be prepared, though, that rooms this reasonable come at the expense of a few amenities—there's no room service, and no mini bar. Not that you'd need one, though, as the food scene is unsurprisingly a huge part of the draw—The Decadente is one of Lisbon's coolest restaurants, and the rooftop bar, The Insólito, is perpetually full of locals grabbing post-work drinks.

[![Image 3](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Alfama-4.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/alfama/memmo-alfama [link_9])

[Memmo Alfama](link_9)

27 Tv. Merceeiras, Alfama

Located in an ancient courtyard in the city’s historic area of Alfama, Memmo Alfama was one of the first boutique hotels in the area, and is still one of the best hotels in Lisbon. From the cozy living room check-in, to its forty-two rooms with amazing views, every inch of the place is intimate and relaxing. The terrace and pool, which also boast incredible views of the river and surrounding city, is the perfect spot for a glass of wine. Plus, the property is only minutes from downtown, and the famous yellow tram (a great way to explore the city) stops nearby, too.

[![Image 4](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/MemmoPrincipeReal2.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/principe-real/memmo-principe-real [link_10])

[Memmo Príncipe Real](link_10)

56 Rua D. Pedro V, Príncipe Real

Hotelier Rodrigo Machaz's third property is set on the top of a hill in the decidedly cool Príncipe Real neighborhood, giving it both a full-circle view of the city (best viewed from the open-air patio of their rooftop bar) and incredible access to some of Lisbon's best shopping and restaurants. Machaz's style is laid back, intimate—only 41 rooms here—and experience-focused, but that doesn't mean his properties skimp on luxury. In addition to the stunning rooftop pool, the hotel is known for high-touch, attentive service, including a concierge with the best recommendations we've come across. Room décor is minimalist but textured, with fur throws at the foot of the bed, floor-to-ceiling paneled headboards, and sleek limestone bathrooms. Leave time for drinks and cocktails at the excellent on-site bar and restaurant.

[![Image 5](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/lapa-palace-4.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/lapa/lapa-palace [link_11])

[Olissippo Lapa Palace Hotel](link_11)

4 Rua do Pau de Bandeira, Lapa

Located on a hilltop in the Lapa District of Lisbon, this historic 19th-century palace-turned-hotel offers stunning views of the Tagus River just a short drive from central Lisbon. The hotel was completely renovated in 2003, yet retains much of the timeless charm it had when it was originally built 170 years ago. You can opt for views of the river, or the regal garden and pool; each room or suite features equally impressive décor that varies from Art Deco to colonial to neo-classic styling.

[![Image 6](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/h10_8-3-19_Piscina-de-di%CC%81a_0038.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/avenida-de-la-libertad/one-palacio-da-anunciada [link_12])

[The One Palácio da Anunciada](link_12)

R. das Portas de Santo Antão 112-134, Avenida da Liberdade

The One Palácio da Anunciada is one of those gorgeously decrepit sixteenth-century palaces that’s had a contemporary vibrancy breathed back into its hallways—while maintaining the integrity of its past. The grand blush marble staircase that sweeps up from the ornate lobby feels all of 400-plus years old, but the guest rooms belong to 2019. Big beds, bigger bathrooms, and Nespresso machines fill the cool, creamy interiors. The spa area is small but mighty with stellar massages and facials on offer alongside an indoor plunge pool and a steam room. High up at the hotel’s crown is the real reason you came here. The hotel’s outdoor pool seems to hover above the city—a rare indulgence in the capital. The surrounding daybeds make the perfect vantage point from which to take in the detailed azulejo (tin-glazed, ceramic tilework) cladding and frescoes on the surrounding buildings.

[![Image 7](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Palacio-Ramalhete-5.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/lapa/palacio-ramalhete [link_13])

[Palacio Ramalhete](link_13)

92 Rua das Janelas Verdes, Lapa

Situated in an exclusive residential section of Lisbon's Lapa District, staying in this small boutique hotel feels like staying in an 18th-century private home, with all of the perks of a modern hospitality. The palace’s secret passageways are fun to explore; the beautiful outdoor pool and bar is the perfect place to unwind at the end of the day, and a generous breakfast buffet is great to help you start the next. Note: If you’re staying here during a busy season, it's best to head to the pool on the earlier side to claim a spot.

[![Image 8](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Pestana-2.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/belem/pestana-palace [link_14])

[Pestana Palace](link_14)

54 Rua Jau, Belém

Once the estate of a cocoa baron, the Pestana Palace has been converted into a hotel and brought back to its former glory, which greets you immediately in the form of an opulent stained glass entryway and the estate's surrounding tropical gardens. Guests get the royal experience here, free to lounge in the indoor and outdoor pools, or dine in the two restaurants that serve Portuguese cuisine with a French twist. While the grounds feel private a secluded, the hotel is near the center of town—it's just seven miles from the Lisbon airport, and close to all the famous monuments of the Belém District.

[![Image 9](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/SantaClara17281.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/alfama/santa-clara-1728 [link_15])

[Santa Clara 1728](link_15)

128 Campo Santa Clara, Alfama

In the center of the city right by the Fiera de Ladra, Lisbon’s flea market, Santa Clara 1728 is a beautiful 18th-century palace that has been transformed into a quiet, romantic sanctuary. Reminiscent of a chic, upscale bed and breakfast, this hotel has six spacious suites and a dining room where the owners (a family who also calls the space home) host delicious dinners open to all guests. Limestone staircases, minimalist wooden furniture, and impressive artwork all complement the beauty of the building itself. Bonus: luxurious, heated bedroom floors, along with views of the Tagus River and National Pantheon.

Restaurants

[![Image 10](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/ACevicheria2.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/principe-real/a-cevicheria [link_16])

[A Cevicheria](link_16)

129 Rua Dom Pedro V, Príncipe Real

A Cevicheria is known for putting a Portuguese spin on Peruvian ceviches (and also for its rather dramatic decór element, a large octopus sculpture that looms over the bar). The rest of the space is white-washed and light-filled, making it a clean slate for the order of choice here—ceviches made with fresh fish that chef Kiko Martins hand-selects from Portuguese markets each morning. And if ceviches are the signature dish here, the pisco sours are the signature cocktail—make sure to get at least one for the table.

[![Image 11](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/a-merendeira-2.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/lapa/a-merendeira [link_17])

[A Merendeira](link_17)

54 Av. 24 de Julho, Lapa

If you're looking for late night sustenance, this is your spot: It's open until 6am, which is something you might require if you find yourself out dancing late. Specialties here include a nice green soup (caldo verde), and fresh baked rolls filled with chorizo and cheese.

[![Image 12](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Alma2.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/chiado/alma [link_18])

[Alma](link_18)

15 Rua Anchieta, Chiado

Henrique Sá Pessoa first opened Alma in 2009—it was his first restaurant, and it catalyzed his career as one of Portugal's few celebrity chefs, opening more restaurants and starring in several cooking shows. Though Alma remained a coveted reservation, Pessoa made the decision to close and relocate the restaurant in 2014, switching up the decór (it's now a warm, mid-century vibe, as though the Eames's decorated an old Portuguese chapel) and recommitting himself to the innovation he was first known for. The gamble paid off—shortly after, the restaurant earned Pessoa his first Michelin star. There are several fixed menus to choose from, although the food can also be ordered a la carte. Either way, have cameras ready, as Pessoa is known for his stunning plating.

[![Image 13](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/16709197939_6dccde61cc_o.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/alfama/cervejaria-ramiro [link_19])

[Cervejaria Ramiro](link_19)

1 Av. Almirante Reis, Alfama

Known for serving some of the best seafood in Lisbon, the brightly lit Cervejaria Ramiro is always bustling with foodies—local and foreign alike—clamoring to try the restaurant's famous clams in garlic sauce, grilled giant tiger shrimp, and percebes (goose barnacles), among a host of other amazing options. While it may seem like you won't have room to try anything but the seafood, save some for their prego, a Portuguese steak sandwich—it's said to be the best in the city. Note: unsurprisingly, this place is pretty popular, so if you want to avoid the line (it's first-come, first-served), it's best to try for an early dinner.

[![Image 14](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/ClubedeJournalistas5.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/lapa/clube-de-jornalistas [link_20])

[Clube de Jornalistas](link_20)

129 Rua Trinas, Lapa

Clube de Jornalistas occupies a converted 18th-century home, but the place to sit is really the gorgeous cobblestone garden/terrace, which is protected on all sides by verdant walls. Both the wine list and the menu are a balance of traditional Portuguese dishes and more international influences—regulars tell us that the lamb burger is the best in town.

[![Image 15](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/ComidadeSanto1.png)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/alcantara/comida-de-santos [link_21])

[Comida de Santo](link_21)

98 R. 1º de Maio, Alcantara

Given the historical connection between the countries, it's no surprise that there are a few great Brazilian restaurants in Lisbon. Comida de Santos airs on the kitschy side, but the grilled meats (and the fries they serve them with) are cooked to perfection, and there are a few great seafood picks on the menu, too. Bonus: The lengthy but very complete wine selection is quite reasonable.

[![Image 16](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/Decadante1.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/bairro-alto/the-decadente [link_22])

[The Decadente](link_22)

81 Rua São Pedro de Alcântara, Bairro Alto

This laid-back spot in the Independente Hostel and Hotel has all the trappings of the quintessential hip restaurant: plywood bar, mismatched vintage chairs for seating, and well-dressed waiters. In the mornings the tables fill up with young locals meeting up for brunch, and in the evenings, there's a DJ in the adjacent bar.

[![Image 17](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/a-travessa-5.jpg)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/madragoa/a-travessa [link_23])

[Fado No Convento](link_23)

12 Travessa do Convento das Bernardas, Madragoa

Occupying a 17th-century convent, Fado No Convento is worth visiting for the ambience alone (particularly if you're here with an S.O., as the old stone and classic arches make for a beautifully romantic setting). Ask for a seat under the stone cloister, where they set up tables for al fresco dining, and if you're visiting in the winter, there are cozy fireplaces indoors. Long-time owner Viviane Durieu is actually Belgian originally, so don't be surprised to find French-speaking expats hanging around, or the appearance of familiar menu items, like moules frites, sole meunière, or foie gras.

[![Image 18](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/05/Palacio-do-Chiado2.png)](https://goop.com/place/portugal/bairro-alto/palacio-chiado [link_24])

[Palácio Chiado](link_24)

70 Rua do Alecrim, Bairro Alto

Entrepreneurs and brothers Duarte Cardoso Pinto and Gustavo and António Paulo Duarte bought Palácio Chiado in 2014, when the 18th-century palace sat in empty disrepair. Over the course of almost two years, they carefully restored the place, breathing new life into the gold-leaf chandeliers, elaborate frescoes and stucco work, and stained glass windows to make a home for their upscale food court program: A series of restaurants and bars spread out over the full two floors of the space. It's worth visiting for the building alone, but the food is deserving of the setting—we like Delisbon for exhaust

*   ![Image 2: Lisbon: The Side of the City I Almost Missed](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi3k224x9aqvccle65CC_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### Lisbon: The Side of the City I Almost Missed

Lisbon is full of famous viewpoints and colorful streets, but I found some of my favorite moments when I wandered beyond the usual tourist route. I started at Mouraria, where narrow lanes, tiled buildings, tiny restaurants, and local life made the neighborhood feel much more authentic than the busy areas around Baixa. I loved simply walking without checking the map every few minutes. Then I headed to LX Factory, a former industrial complex transformed into a creative hub filled with shops, cafés, art, and restaurants. The old factory atmosphere mixed with modern creativity gave it a completely different personality. My third discovery was Jardim do Torel, a small hillside garden where I could sit quietly and look across Lisbon’s rooftops. It was the kind of place I would have easily walked past if I hadn’t been exploring slowly. I still visited Belém Tower, Jerónimos Monastery, São Jorge Castle, Praça do Comércio, Alfama, Santa Justa Lift, and Miradouro da Senhora do Monte, but these three places showed me a more relaxed Lisbon and that was the side I enjoyed most. #lisbon #portugal  ![Image 3: Rani Mamahit](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0a246224x9a2fg33e0413_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)Rani Mamahit __ 9    
*   ![Image 4: Places I visit in Lisbon🇵🇹🚋](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi1b224x9aaplcy95068_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### Places I visit in Lisbon🇵🇹🚋

🏛️ Jerónimos Monastery If you’re visiting Lisbon, I really think this is a must-visit. It’s honestly beautiful from every angle. The monastery is one of the most important examples of Portuguese Manueline architecture and is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The cloister inside was my favorite part — so many beautiful details, arches, and really nice light for photos. If you love photography, definitely give yourself enough time here because there are so many beautiful corners to explore. The current entrance fee for the monastery is €18. 🏰 Praça do Comércio One of Lisbon’s most iconic squares, right by the Tagus River. The huge open square is surrounded by beautiful yellow buildings, with the statue of King José I in the middle and the impressive Arco da Rua Augusta behind it. It’s one of those places where you arrive and immediately feel like, “Okay, I’m really in Lisbon now.” 🌊 Cais das Colunas Just walk from Praça do Comércio towards the river and you’ll find these steps leading down to the water with two stone columns. In the past, this was an important arrival point for people entering Lisbon by boat. I really liked how open and peaceful it felt here, with a wide view over the Tagus River. Definitely worth walking down for a few photos. 🛗 Santa Justa Lift This one really caught my attention! I was just walking around the city and suddenly saw this huge old iron lift standing between the buildings and thought, “What is that?” 😂 It was actually built in the early 1900s to connect the lower Baixa area with the higher Carmo area — very useful in such a hilly city. The lift is currently temporarily closed, but you can still see and photograph the beautiful iron structure from outside. ⛪ Lisbon Cathedral (Sé de Lisboa) One of the oldest and most important churches in Lisbon, with a history going all the way back to the 12th century. One of my favorite things here was seeing the classic yellow tram passing right in front of the cathedral. If you catch the timing right, it makes such a perfect Lisbon photo. 🏘️ Alfama I really loved walking around Alfama. The neighborhood is so colorful and full of character, with old houses, beautiful azulejo tiles, tiny balconies, narrow streets and even laundry hanging outside the windows. I love that it still feels like a real neighborhood where people actually live, rather than somewhere created just for tourists. And if you love taking photos, almost every little street has something interesting to photograph. 🌅 Miradouro de Santa Luzia If you’re walking around Alfama, don’t miss this viewpoint. You get such a beautiful view over Lisbon’s orange rooftops with the Tagus River in the background. I had so much fun walking around this area. It felt like I was getting lost inside a little orange-roofed village. The viewpoint itself is also really pretty, with flowers and traditional blue azulejo panels. 🚋 Lisbon Tram & Tram 28 You can’t really think of Lisbon without picturing its little yellow trams. The most famous is Tram 28, which travels through several historic neighborhoods and passes many of the city’s landmarks. What makes it special is seeing these small vintage trams climbing steep hills and squeezing through incredibly narrow streets between old buildings. Even if you don’t ride it, spotting one passing by is part of the Lisbon experience. 🍰 Alcôa – Chiado A lovely place to try traditional Portuguese conventual sweets, which are often made with egg yolks, sugar and almonds. There were so many interesting pastries to choose from, including Torrão Real and Delícia de Amêndoa. Personally, I found the sweets here quite sweet 😆, so if you’re not a big sweet tooth, I’d recommend ordering a few different ones and sharing them. 🧁 Confeitaria Nacional One of Lisbon’s historic pastry shops, dating all the way back to 1829. You’ll find plenty of traditional Portuguese pastries here, including Pastel de Nata. I think part of the experience is not only trying the desserts but also sitting inside a pastry shop that has been part of Lisbon for almost 200 years. ☕ Fábrica Coffee Roasters – Chiado And of course, coffee! I visited the branch on Rua das Flores 63. It’s a specialty coffee shop and a really nice place to take a break after walking around Lisbon — especially because this city has so many hills! After a long day of walking, sitting down with a good cup of coffee felt pretty perfect. 🇵🇹 For me, Lisbon isn’t only about the big landmarks. I really enjoyed all the little things in between — colorful houses, azulejo-covered walls, yellow trams, tiny streets, orange rooftops, Portuguese sweets and stopping for coffee along the way. It’s such a fun city to simply walk around, get a little lost and see what you find. #lisbon  ![Image 5: Giftmetrip](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0a26h224x97uhbjzz522B_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)Giftmetrip __ 30    
*   ![Image 6: Lisbon - Hills and Navigation](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi4y224x9aq9kers28CF_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### Lisbon - Hills and Navigation

Lisbon is a mountain town full of storytelling, and the distance between the old city and the Atlantic Ocean always evokes imagination. On this two-day trip, walk along the stone roads up the hills, slowly feel Portugal’s maritime history, Mediterranean atmosphere and unbeatable sunset views, and finally understand why everyone recommends an in-depth trip to Lisbon. 🗓️Itinerary: Day 1: Alphama Old Town — St. Lucia Observation Deck — St. Jorge Castle Day 2: Jeronimos Monastery—Beren Tower—Sailboat in the evening to watch the sunset Day 1 Highlights: The first stop is Alfama Old Town, an area that retains the most pristine taste of Lisbon. The narrow and winding streets, the walls covered with colored tiles and nostalgic authentic small shops, the aroma of coffee and the ever-present Fado song makes people linger. Alfama is open all day year round, no tickets required, it is recommended to plan your route in advance, don’t be afraid of getting lost and you may encounter surprise alleys! Next stop is the Santa Lucia Observation Deck, which is recommended to go up at dusk, Largo de Santa Luzia, 1100-487 Lisboa. From here you can overlook the Red Roof and Tagus River, which is super good for taking pictures at sunrise, sunset or noon. Then walk up St. Jorge Castle, R. de Santa Cruz do Castelo, 1100-129 Lisboa. The castle is built on a hilltop and overlooks the best view of the entire city of Lisbon. It is recommended to go early in advance, there are fewer entrants before noon. The castle has different opening hours, 9:00-18:00 in winter and until 21:00 in summer, tickets are 191.5 (Portuguese currency). Please note that the museum will be closed on different holidays. When buying tickets, you can ask the staff to get a map for easy tours of the different exhibition areas and towers. Day 2 Featured Highlights: Geronimos Monastery, Praça do Império 1400-206 Lisboa. This World Heritage Site blends Manuel style with Gothic architectural details, very grand and every inch worth taking pictures. The lobby and cloister have the most outstanding views, and it is recommended to go before the doors open to avoid group guests. The monastery is closed on Mondays, other times 09:30-17:30 (last entry 17:00), tickets 150.0. Stop 2 Belem Tower, Av. Brasília, 1400-038 Lisboa. As a landmark of Lisbon, it is perfect for arrangement with the monastery. The appearance is like a grand little fortress, very photogenic from different angles, remember to bring sunscreen! Belenta is closed on Mondays and some public holidays, the rest of the days are open from 09:30-17:30, tickets are 116.0. The last stop is the unmissable sailing sunset experience in Lisbon, departing from the Belém district pier, enjoying the most magnificent coastline and golden sky along the way, very relaxing, while far away from the hustle and bustle of the city, great for slowing down and feeling the beauty of the journey. Practical tips: 1. The city is mainly walking, it is recommended to wear comfortable sneakers and bring water and snacks. 2. More mountain roads, pay attention to mobile phone/camera battery, check in along the way. 3. Always for European cities, valuables keep carefully. 4. Most attractions are closed on Mondays. 5. Early ticket purchase is recommended, especially during the peak summer tourist season, to reduce unnecessary queue times. #Lisbon Trip #Hill Beauty #Portugal Must See #Navigation History #Photo Hotspots ![Image 7: VisualStorytellingThroughPhotography](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0a22q224x9ana8mc4158C_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)VisualStorytellingThroughPhotography __ 3    
*   ![Image 8: Arco da Rua Augusta Lisbon](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi0h424x9a9y4x903DB2_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### Arco da Rua Augusta Lisbon

I lived in Lisbon for 8 years and never climbed this iconic arch. Biggest mistake of my life. Honestly, I have no excuse. I walked under the Arco da Rua Augusta more times than I can count, always in a rush, always thinking "I'll do it another time." Eight years living in Lisbon. It took a Trip.com booking to finally make me stop and look up. The arch was built to celebrate Lisbon's reconstruction after the catastrophic 1755 earthquake. It took nearly 100 years to complete. Standing at the top, looking out over Praça do Comércio and the Tejo River with the whole city laid out beneath you, you start to understand why it mattered so much to get it right. I booked through Trip.com and it was genuinely straightforward. Found the attraction on the app, picked my time slot, got the voucher on my phone, and exchanged it for the ticket at the entrance in under two minutes. The kind of smooth experience that makes you wonder why travel ever feels complicated. If you're visiting Lisbon and only have a few hours, this is the one. Go late afternoon when the light hits the river and everything turns gold. You'll thank yourself later. Practical info: located at Praça do Comércio in Baixa, right at the waterfront. Book in advance, especially in summer. #LisbonTravel #VisitLisbon #ArcoRuaAugusta #Lisbon #PortugalTravel #TravelEurope  Mirelats __ 21    
*   ![Image 9: Autumn in Lisbon: Best Food 🇵🇹](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi6b424x9apfvd6gEC54_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### Autumn in Lisbon: Best Food 🇵🇹

We visited Lisbon in December last year for a quick recharge before the end of the year, and off-season is truly the best kept secret. The weather was so mild that we had breakfast outside in the sun every morning. The summer rush is gone, so you get genuine local interactions, empty streets, and fresh oranges hanging from every tree. Here are three spots we loved: 🧁 Fresh Pastéis at Manteigaria: Watching the bakers work behind the glass counter while eating warm custard tarts dusted with cinnamon is unbeatable. Pair it with hot chocolate! 🍷 Solar dos Bicos for Local Seafood: Authentic, relaxed, and hearty. We had fresh grilled fish and bacalhau without needing reservations weeks ahead.We were surrounded by very friendly locals and really enjoyed the ambiance! 🍊 Alfama Courtyards: Stumble into hidden square terraces shaded by ripe orange trees for a breakfasr with freshly squizzed orange juice. We could taste C-vitamin there! Best to know before your departure: Best time to walk is late morning when the sun hits the squares. Pack comfortable sneakers with good grip. The traditional stone pavements are notoriously slick. Take your camera with you! Colors are the best in winter and you'll enjoy beautiful traditional streets. Without any tourists! #lisbon #localfood #foodtravel #autumnbeauty #pastéisdenata  FlorelieTrip __ 3

### Sintra Palace Day Trip + Evening World Cup at Volta do Duche Café, Lisbon Side — Fairy-Tale Sightsee

#travelwithfootball Sintra is a non-negotiable on any Portugal itinerary, but most tourists rush back to Lisbon and crash. My move? Spend the day touring Quinta da Regaleira and Palácio Nacional de Sintra, then walk down to Volta do Duche (the old tram turnaround area near the station) where several terraced cafés—Café Saudade, Fábrica da Nata Sintra, and the small esplanadas facing the valley—have TVs showing live sport once the sun goes down. I did exactly this: finished the initiation well and spiral staircase by 17:30, grabbed a travesseiroalmond pastry, descended to Volta do Duche, and claimed an outdoor heater table at a corner café with a clear view of their wall-mounted screen. Ordered a Sagres and watched Portugal's group stage opener with a mix of day-trippers and Sintra locals still walking their dogs past the viewpoint. Trains run from Sintra to Rossio (Lisbon) until around 00:30 in summer—check CP (Comboios de Portugal) timetables; if you miss the last one, Ubers to central Lisbon run €25–35. Stay overnight in a Sintra B&B (many converted quintas offer great value) and you can linger even longer. I recommend pairing Sintra's UNESCO magic with an evening match here because the light over the green hills at dusk is unreal, the cafés are far less frantic than Lisbon's Chiado/Bairro Alto, and you feel like you've hacked the tourist trail—sightsee all day, then slide seamlessly into World Cup mode without changing cities. Cool mountain air, fairy-tale backdrop, cold Portuguese lager, live football—that's #travelwithfootball with a twist of romance.  tyy6

São Jorge CastleIt is one of the ancient buildings in Lisbon and a major historical monument and tourist attraction in Lisbon. The castle is built onAlfamaThe high point of the area was a fortress when the Moors occupied Lisbon in the Middle Ages. Located on a commanding hillside, its presence can be seen from almost every corner of Lisbon. The castle originally belonged to the earlier Visigoths. After the Moorish invasion, it underwent large-scale expansion, and its walls, up to 8 m thick, still impress with their grandeur today. Here, people can better appreciate the city's architectural art, whether fromAlfamaTo the futuristic castles and drawbridges in the distant city, or in the urbanCarmo churchThe open-air ruins can be seen at a glance. National monument The architectural complex known as Lisbon castle and Lisbon city walls was classified as a national monument under the decree issued on June 16, 1910. The monument is owned by the Portuguese state and was temporarily transferred to Lisbon city hall on September 13, 1934, with the complete transfer finalized on May 31, 1942. On June 8, 1979, the revised terms of transfer for São Jorge Castle were officially enacted. Following the resolution of the Lisbon municipal council in October 1995, São Jorge Castle was placed under the management of the municipal company Empresa de Bairros Históricos de Lisboa (EBAHL). In 2003, this management responsibility was transferred to the municipal company Empresa de Gestão de Equipamentos e Animação Cultural (EGEAC). The site consists of a castle, the ruins of the Alcázar palace, the Plaza de Armas, a spacious viewing platform overlooking the entire city, a museum exhibition area, an archaeological exhibition area, several garden areas, and the city walls. The monument covers an area of approx. 4 hectares, surrounded by a massive perimeter wall and city walls, with one section of the wall coinciding with part of the boundary of Lisbon's old castle. Space and view In the past, there were no trees inside or outside the city walls; even if there were, the quantity was far less than today. In the days when the castle was merely a fortress to be conquered, it was absolutely unacceptable to provide the enemy with any tools for climbing or even setting fires, thereby facilitating their siege. The castle garden was built in the 1950s and is one of the earliest view architecture works in Portugal. Its designer, architect Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles, conceived this garden precisely when the castle completely ceased its military use, aiming to complement the historic site while providing visitors with a highly comfortable leisure area.

### Lisbon: The Side of the City I Almost Missed

Lisbon is full of famous viewpoints and colorful streets, but I found some of my favorite moments when I wandered beyond the usual tourist route. I started at Mouraria, where narrow lanes, tiled buildings, tiny restaurants, and local life made the neighborhood feel much more authentic than the busy areas around Baixa. I loved simply walking without checking the map every few minutes. Then I headed to LX Factory, a former industrial complex transformed into a creative hub filled with shops, cafés, art, and restaurants. The old factory atmosphere mixed with modern creativity gave it a completely different personality. My third discovery was Jardim do Torel, a small hillside garden where I could sit quietly and look across Lisbon’s rooftops. It was the kind of place I would have easily walked past if I hadn’t been exploring slowly. I still visited Belém Tower, Jerónimos Monastery, São Jorge Castle, Praça do Comércio, Alfama, Santa Justa Lift, and Miradouro da Senhora do Monte, but these three places showed me a more relaxed Lisbon and that was the side I enjoyed most. #lisbon #portugal

### Arco da Rua Augusta Lisbon

I lived in Lisbon for 8 years and never climbed this iconic arch. Biggest mistake of my life. Honestly, I have no excuse. I walked under the Arco da Rua Augusta more times than I can count, always in a rush, always thinking "I'll do it another time." Eight years living in Lisbon. It took a Trip.com booking to finally make me stop and look up. The arch was built to celebrate Lisbon's reconstruction after the catastrophic 1755 earthquake. It took nearly 100 years to complete. Standing at the top, looking out over Praça do Comércio and the Tejo River with the whole city laid out beneath you, you start to understand why it mattered so much to get it right. I booked through Trip.com and it was genuinely straightforward. Found the attraction on the app, picked my time slot, got the voucher on my phone, and exchanged it for the ticket at the entrance in under two minutes. The kind of smooth experience that makes you wonder why travel ever feels complicated. If you're visiting Lisbon and only have a few hours, this is the one. ### Lisbon.

Lisbon is one of Europe’s most beautiful, romantic, and budget-friendly capitals. Perched on seven hills along the Atlantic coast, the city boasts stunning "Miradouros" (viewpoints) hidden around every corner, charming pastel buildings, vintage trams, and fresh, delicious seafood. By 2026, Lisbon has perfected the blend of historic charm and chic modern cafes, all while remaining significantly more affordable than other European hubs. Must-Visit Highlights in Lisbon: Ride the Vintage Tram 28: This iconic yellow tram zigs and zags through narrow, hilly streets. Try to catch it early in the morning to beat the long queues. Sunset at Castelo de São Jorge: This ancient hilltop castle offers a 360-degree panorama of Lisbon and the Tagus River. The atmosphere here at dusk is incredibly romantic. Discover History in Belém: Take a train west to visit the Belém Tower and Jerónimos Monastery—UNESCO World Heritage sites that showcase the Golden Age of Discovery. Don’t Miss the Original Egg Tarts: Lisbon is the birthplace of this world-famous treat. We recommend visiting Pastéis de Belém, the legendary bakery that has been serving them since 1837.

### Portugal: One Country, Endless Adventures You’ll Want to Experience Again

Hi family! Portugal is hands-down one of Europe’s ultimate bucket-list destinations, and trust me, you’ll wanna come back for round two (or three! 😏). From buzzing cities to wild cliffs and cozy old towns, every corner is pure vibez. You get legendary wine, food that’s honestly 🤤, and locals so warm you’ll wanna move in. Portugal’s so diverse, every day brings a whole new adventure. One morning you’re hopping yellow trams around Lisbon, by lunch you’re soaking up that ocean air on the Algarve’s epic cliffs, and by dinner you’re sipping Port beside the magical Douro in Porto. It’s all good vibes and seriously dreamy views! How Long Should You Stay? 🗓️ If it’s your first time, 7-10 days gives you time to soak it all up (and trust me, you’ll want even more). Here’s a fire sample itinerary you’ll love: 3 days in Lisbon (color, hills & those epic views!) 1 day in Sintra (hello, fairytale castles) 2 days in Porto (wine caves & riverside strolls) 2–3 days in the Algarve (beaches for days) Got extra time? Hit up the Douro Valley (wine, baby!), Évora for medieval feels, or jet off to Madeira for that tropical getaway. When to Visit for Max Vibes🗓️ Portugal slays all year, but April-June and September-October are chef’s kiss, perfect weather, less crowding and prices way easier on the wallet. Beach obsessed? July and August bring that sunshine energy, just expect more peeps around! Winter? Still pretty mild—way better than most of Europe—so don’t sleep on a winter wander. Getting Round the Country👉🏼 Portugal’s transport game is on point. Zip from Lisbon to Porto by high-speed train or jump on comfy buses to pretty much anywhere. Hitting up the Algarve, Douro, or those off-the-beaten-track gems? Renting a car = big freedom vibes. Roads are solid and super easy to drive! Lisbon: Your Dreamy Launchpad🫶🏼 Lisbon’s energy is a 12/10: pastel colors, steep hills, and unreal miradouros (viewpoints) everywhere you look. You’ve gotta hit: Belém Tower (Av. Brasília, 1400-038 Lisbon) Jerónimos Monastery (Praça do Império 1400-206 Lisbon, 10am–6:30pm) Praça do Comércio (Downtown vibes) Alfama (wander & listen for that Fado music) Hopping Tram 28 🚋 Castelo de São Jorge (Rua de Santa Cruz, 1100-129 Lisbon) Time Out Market (A foodie heaven: Av. 24 de Julho 49) My TOP tip: get lost in Alfama at sunset—music drifting from tiny taverns, golden light, pure magic. Porto: Laidback & Photo-Ready Porto is a total switch-up. It’s chill, wildly photogenic, and the wine? Next level. Hit up: Ribeira District (riverside cuteness everywhere) Dom Luís I Bridge (epic for sunset strolls) Livraria Lello (seriously magical bookstore, Rua das Carmelitas 144) São Bento Station (tiles for days) Porto Cathedral (Terreiro da Sé) Wine cellars in Vila Nova de Gaia (sip the legendary Port!) Best hack: cross the Dom Luís I Bridge pre-sunset—the views will blow up your IG. Sintra: Fairytale Central Sintra is a dreamy day trip from Lisbon, don’t skip it! You’ll get: Palácio da Pena (Estrada da Pena, 2710-609 Sintra, arrive at 9am or earlier to beat busloads of tourists!) Quinta da Regaleira (love the gardens and mysterious tunnels) Moorish Castle (views for days) Pack comfy shoes and channel your inner royal for those castle walks. The Algarve: Beachside Bliss The Algarve’s all about those glowing cliffs, Insta-worthy caves and turquoise tides. Don’t miss:✅ Benagil Cave (Accessible from Benagil Beach, just east of Carvoeiro—book a boat tour!) Praia da Marinha (supermodel beach vibes) Ponta da Piedade (jaw-dropping rock formations, near Lagos) Lagos/Carvoeiro/Albufeira (cute towns & epic sunsets) Boat tours are a MUST—the sea caves are unreal and way better by water. Photography Pro Tips📸 Lisbon: Sunrise at Miradouro da Senhora do Monte Porto: Walk Dom Luís I Bridge at golden hour Sintra: Snap Pena Palace from the trails, less crowds, killer perspective! Algarve: Golden hour makes those cliffs look like melted gold … don’t miss it. What To Eat (and Eat and Eat…)🍛🥘 The food here is on another level. You HAVE to try: Pastéis de Nata (flaky, creamy goodness) Bacalhau à Brás (iconic salted cod dish) Grilled sardines (simple, sooo good!) Cataplana (seafood stew, toasty and rich) Francesinha (Porto’s famous meat + cheese sandwich, bring your appetite) Polvo à Lagareiro (tender octopus, next level) Bifana sandwiches (spicy pork snack) And don’t forget a pastel de nata + espresso—a life-changing dessert/coffee duo! Drink Game Port Wine (try it at the cellars in Gaia, Porto) Vinho Verde (zesty, perfect for beach days) Ginjinha (Lisbon’s berry liqueur) Moscatel de Setúbal (sweet wine you’ll crave back home) Wine lovers, Douro Valley day trip is mandatory. Secret Tips Most People Miss👌🏼 Hop Tram 28 before 9am, no queues, no elbowing. Check out smaller miradouros for peaceful views way better than the famous ones! For the best Porto sunset, cross into Vila Nova de Gaia, you’ll get a postcard-perfect skyline moment. If you don’t want the couvert (bread/cheese) in restaurants, just say no thanks, it’s not free, heads up! Algarve beaches = lotsa steps, so bring proper shoes. (Flips and long stairs are not a vibe.) Snag a Lisbon or Sintra city pass if you’re monument-hopping (saves time AND money). What to Skip 🚫 Trying to do Lisbon AND Porto in one weekend—trust me, you’ll want more chill time. Tourist trap restaurants right next to the sights—always check reviews! Slippery stone sidewalks + steep hills = sneakers are your BFF. Always validate your metro/train ticket (otherwise fines = not fun). Watch out for electronic tolls if you’re driving—no booths, so don’t miss payment instructions! Ultimate Portugal Vibes✨ Portugal overdelivers every dang time. It’s got mountains, beaches, castles, jaw-dropping old towns, and the kindest people ever. ### Come to Hailing Island in August! New pool villa opens on 8.14

When visiting Hailing Island, you always want to fit in four or five spots in one day. Stay at the Ten-Mile Silver Beach villa and spend the afternoon by the pool—kids actually have more fun that way. This villa is better suited for👇 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 family vacations | friends traveling together | groups enjoying the sea view 🚗 free parking 🏡 multiple room types to choose from based on number of guests ✨ The biggest perks of staying in a villa ▪️ private pool, no need to pack a big bag every time you want to swim ▪️ multiple people stay in the same villa, making it easy to gather and watch the kids ▪️ spend the day at Ten-Mile Silver Beach and rest at the villa when it’s hot ▪️ at night, sing, play mahjong, or have a barbecue based on the actual villa amenities 📍 Nearby spots on the way: Ten-Mile Silver Beach Dajiao Bay Mawei Island Xincheng Fishing Village Shenyu Souvenirs 📌 The number of rooms and entertainment facilities vary by villa. Check the actual setup before booking. It’s okay to skip a couple of attractions. If the kids have enough fun and the adults aren’t exhausted, the trip is a success.  ![Image 3: ku_Xanthe_](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi1012000c2myt6b8EA6_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)ku_Xanthe_   
*   ![Image 4: A must-visit glamping spot for families](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi1m12000tqhij4uA599_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### A must-visit glamping spot for families

 Want to deeply embrace nature? Xingyi Yuntun Starry Sky Glamping Hotel is definitely your top choice! I was completely won over by this stay! Bringing the kids to stay among the forest and stars, far from the hustle and bustle of the city—this is the ideal family vacation! 📍 [Location & Transportation] The hotel is located deep within the Xingyi Yuntun National Forest Health Base. It offers excellent privacy, making it perfect for short family trips. Transportation is very convenient; it is about a 36-minute drive from Xingyi Airport, and the roads are smooth for driving. You can reach it in about 40 minutes by car from downtown Xingyi, and it is only about 30 minutes from the Xingyi High-Speed Railway Station. Whether you are driving or arriving by high-speed rail, it is very convenient. Simply navigate to "Xingyi Yuntun Starry Sky Glamping Hotel" to reach the park entrance directly. There are dedicated parking spaces within the park, making parking very easy. 🏕 [Hotel Environment] This is a hidden treasure of a glamping retreat tucked away in the deep mountains. Everywhere you look, you see lush forests and rolling green hills, with fresh, healing air. The hotel rooms are scattered among the lawns and forests, arranged in an orderly and uncrowded manner. The signature wooden treehouses are full of atmosphere, with eco-friendly wooden architecture that blends into the natural mountain forest, feeling both gentle and healing. The most stunning feature is the Starry Sky Tent room, which comes with a panoramic transparent roof. You can lie in bed and gaze at the galaxy, wake up to the forest breeze, and spend the night accompanied by the stars—an immersive stay in nature. 🛏 [Room Facilities] The rooms feature a minimalist, healing wood design. The entire house is furnished with high-quality solid wood furniture, and the decor is clean, tidy, and full of atmosphere. The bedding is soft, skin-friendly, and has just the right firmness, ensuring a super comfortable sleep for both adults and children. The details show high-end quality; the rooms are equipped with Dyson hair dryers, and the toiletries are a full set of Hermès products, adding a touch of exquisite detail. The rooms are fully equipped with excellent lighting and ventilation, offering a comfortable and high-end living experience that rivals top-tier resorts. 🌌 [Featured Experiences] This hotel offers incredibly high playability, covering all your vacation needs in one stop! Far from city lights and with almost no light pollution, it is an excellent spot for stargazing. The room skylights offer a fantastic view, and at night, you can look up at the brilliant starry sky. The hotel is also equipped with professional astronomical telescopes, and staff members lead tours to explain constellations, creating a wonderful atmosphere. There are many family-friendly projects specifically designed for children, including pottery making, sketching, flower arranging, and pinecone DIY. These rich, hands-on activities are great for developing children's skills. The park also has an exclusive children's play area and a petting zoo where kids can feed small animals up close. They won't be bored for a whole day, which is a huge relief for parents. There are also plenty of leisure activities for adults. In the morning, you can hike or cycle along the forest trails and breathe in the fresh air of this natural oxygen bar. In the evening, there are romantic outdoor movies and lively bonfires. In addition, outdoor activities like laser tag, horseback riding, and archery are all available, making it perfect for family interaction or trips with friends. 🍽 [Dining & Cuisine] The hotel has its own exclusive restaurant with a rich selection of dishes that cater to both adults and children. You can find authentic Guizhou-style cuisine—spicy, sour, and fresh—as well as refined Western food with a balanced mix of meat and vegetables. A buffet breakfast is included daily, offering a wide variety of fresh and delicious options to satisfy the whole family. In the evening, you can book an outdoor starry sky BBQ in advance. Enjoying a BBQ while feeling the mountain breeze and watching the stars creates a wonderful atmosphere and a true sense of vacation ritual. 💁 [Thoughtful Service] The hotel's service is truly detailed and thoughtful. The staff is warm and gentle, and the check-in process is efficient and quick. If you have a lot of luggage, the staff will proactively help you carry it and guide you throughout the process. The park covers a large area, and the guest rooms are spread out, so the hotel provides sightseeing carts to shuttle guests between the lobby and their rooms at any time. You don't have to walk, which makes traveling with the elderly and children stress-free. There are also abundant resources for sightseeing around the hotel. In your spare time, you can visit the famous Wanfenglin Scenic Area to see the stunning mountain and water scenery, or stroll through the Yuntun International Ecological Sports Park to get close to nature and relax. Escape the city hustle and head to the forest and stars. This hidden glamping hotel in the Xingyi forest is truly perfect for a family vacation! With its immersive nature experience, rich activities, and thoughtful service, it is perfect for a short family trip or a weekend getaway. Pack your bags and bring your family!  ![Image 5: Dragonfire3210](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi1212000c2n5h3v8AA8_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)Dragonfire3210 __ 4    
*   ![Image 6: This is my favorite city so far! ](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi2u12000tqvb5vyB247_W_640_0_R5_Q80.jpg?proc=source/trip) 
### This is my favorite city so far!

A coastal city living room transformed from a century-old port, open to the public for free. With the Yantai landmark sign, rose staircase, and white carousel, it's packed with popular photo spots. Facing the bay with a view of the Yantai Mountain Lighthouse, the sunset over the "orange sea" is absolutely divine. It connects to Yantai Mountain, Chaoyang Street, and Suochengli, offering a one-stop destination for old town and sea views. Perfect for leisurely walks, families, and couples. 📅 2-day, 1-night relaxed itinerary 🚄 Transportation: ✅ High-speed train: Take the train to Yantai Station. It's a 10-minute walk from the station to Zhifu Bay Square, with a prime location. ✅ Driving: Navigate to "Zhifu Bay Square." Paid parking is available. ✅ Bus: Take the No. 17 double-decker coastal sightseeing bus and sit on the top deck to enjoy the coastline views. 🏨 Accommodation: We recommend choosing a hotel or homestay near Yantai Station or Chaoyang Street in Zhifu District for convenient travel and dining. Day 1 | Zhifu Bay Square > Yantai Mountain > Chaoyang Street: Explore the old town and watch the sunset ▫️ 2:00 PM Arrive at Zhifu Bay Square Visit popular photo spots like the Yantai landmark wall, rose waterfall staircase, white carousel, and the Tangtangmiao ship. Stroll along the coastal boardwalk and watch the boats go by. Optional paid activity: Sailing trip to chase the sunset and feed seagulls at sea (approx. 40 minutes). You can buy seafood at Hongli Fish Market, which offers on-site cooking services at a great value. ▫️ 4:00 PM Walk to Yantai Mountain Scenic Area Explore the century-old consulate buildings. If you have time, climb the lighthouse for a panoramic view of Zhifu Bay. ▫️ 5:30 PM Stroll along Chaoyang Street A district of Republican-era Western-style buildings, filled with creative shops and cafes. Enjoy a leisurely walk. ▫️ 6:30 PM Return to Zhifu Bay Square to wait for the "orange sea" sunset and enjoy the harbor night lights as darkness falls. Day 2 | Suochengli > Coastal leisure, relaxed departure ▫️ Morning: Explore the Suochengli historical district, experience the local life of Yantai's old town, and visit the ancient alleys and Xuanhua Gate. ▫️ Noon: Taste local delicacies: Mackerel dumplings, sea worm rice, Yantai menzi, and Penglai noodles. ▫️ Afternoon: Take a walk at Coastal Square. If you have time, head to Fisherman's Wharf before departing. 📌 Travel tips ▪️ Tickets: Zhifu Bay Square is free. Admission to Yantai Mountain is free, but there is a fee to climb the lighthouse. The sailing trip is an optional paid activity. ▪️ Best time to visit: After 2:00 PM to avoid the midday sun and wait for the sunset glow. ▪️ Clothing: It can be windy by the sea, so bring a light jacket. Use sun protection, and light-colored clothing looks better in photos. ▪️ Food: For seafood, prioritize Hongli Fish Market for cooking or local long-standing restaurants, and avoid overpriced stalls in tourist areas. ▪️ Note: The square is near the pier. If traveling with children, keep an eye on them and stay away from the water. It gets crowded during sunset on holidays. ![Image 7: The Traveling Feast](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/1mi0j12000b8d1nynCD56_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)The Traveling Feast __ 24

### Beijing's Hidden Gem! China National Film Museum: Next-Level Art, Free Admission! 。

Photographers, content creators, and movie buffs, you absolutely can't miss this! 🍿 Today, we're checking out the China National Film Museum (中国电影博物馆), the largest film museum in the world! Trust me, it’s not just about cool Chinese cinematic history; the real showstopper is the "4-story high, 360-degree giant LED screen" that immerses you in a futuristic, space-like virtual reality. It's totally next-level, and every angle is insanely Instagrammable! 🤩📸 ✨ Absolute Must-See Highlights! 🌌 360-Degree Giant LED Screen Exhibition Hall (1st Floor): The Vibe: A 4-story LED screen wraps entirely around you, projecting breathtaking scenes—from the cosmic Milky Way 🌌 and the deep ocean 🐋 to lush summer forests 🍃 and epic snowy mountains. It feels like stepping straight into a fantasy movie! 📸 Best Photo Op: Head up to the connecting stairs on the 2nd or 3rd floor, whip out your ultra-wide lens, and shoot downward. You'll capture both yourself and the massive graphic floor below for a jaw-dropping shot! ⭐ Giant Red Star Architecture: The Vibe: The exterior and entrance feature a massive red five-pointed star design, symbolizing the history and legacy of Chinese cinema. It's incredibly cool and modern. 🎞️ A Century of Film History Zone: The Vibe: Stroll past statues of cinema pioneers, dazzling light exhibits, and the timeline of Chinese film from 1905 to 2005. It gives off a neat retro-meets-sci-fi aesthetic. 📌 Pro-Tips for Your Visit ⚠️ Super Important: Admission is "Totally Free!" 🆓 But you MUST book your tickets online in advance. 📍 Location: China National Film Museum (中国电影博物馆) ⏰ Hours: Tuesday - Sunday, 09:00 AM - 05:00 PM (⚠️ Ticket distribution and entry end at 04:30 PM, and the 2nd & 3rd-floor exhibits close right at 05:00 PM on the dot. Get there early!) 🚫 Closed: Every Monday 🚇 Getting There: Take Subway Line 14 to either Wangjing South Station (望京南站) or Jiangtai Station (将台站). From there, hopping in a ride-share (DiDi) for about 10-15 minutes is your best bet! 🚗💨 🇨🇳 🇨🇳 🇨🇳 🎬 📝 📸 ✈️ DIY Travel 🗺️  ![Image 9: เที่ยวกับ Bunny](https://ak-d.tripcdn.com/images/0a26c224x9ag6s0r0E2E9_W_100_0_R5_Q90.jpg)เที่ยวกับ Bunny __ 73

### Hulun Lake | I can't believe there's a sea hidden at the end of the grasslands

Head to Hulun Lake at sunset At the end of the grasslands, there really is a sea~ On one side, the vast and magnificent cliffs overlooking the lake; On the other, the gentle tranquility of the lake, cattle, and sheep🐮 When the wind blows from the lake, all fatigue just melts away~ ㅤ 📍Location: Private pasture on the west bank of Hulun Lake (cliff viewpoint) Large stretches of pristine grassland reach right to the lake's edge, with cliffs along the shore and cattle and sheep scattered by the water—this is the scenery captured in the video. There are no crowded tourists, and you can get a full, panoramic view of this lake that looks just like the ocean. How to get there❓ 🔖Direction: From Manzhouli towards Jalainur, along the west bank of Hulun Lake. ⚠Important: This is a private pasture and belongs to the herdsmen; you cannot just drive in. There is usually a contact number at the pasture entrance. Communicate with the herdsmen in advance, pay a small entrance fee, and get permission before entering. 🚗Transportation: Must drive yourself / charter a car; there is no public transportation. Mostly dirt roads, so an SUV is preferred. Be cautious with small cars, as they can easily get stuck in the mud on rainy days. ㅤ Best time: Sunset🌅 Arrive 2 hours before sunset. The sunlight turns a warm gold, the lake surface takes on an orange hue, the contours of the cliffs are most defined, and the silhouettes of the cattle and sheep are stunning. ### I don't think I'll ever forget autumn in the Greater Khingan Mountains

### Qiandao Lake is legendary in autumn: A complete guide to Huangshan Jian + Meifeng Island + Moonlight Island #StrollQiandao

As the autumn breeze sweeps across the mountains of western Zhejiang, thousands of islands are scattered across the vast expanse of emerald water. In autumn, Qiandao Lake transforms the entire landscape into a grand land art exhibition. To truly appreciate the autumn colors of Qiandao Lake, you must venture out onto the water. Take a cruise across the clear, emerald waves, where islands stretch out like a painting. The two core highlights of Qiandao Lake, Huangshan Jian and Meifeng Island, hold the most breathtaking panoramic views of this autumn landscape. Take the cable car for a slow ascent to the Huangshan Jian observation deck. Looking out into the distance, over 90 natural islands are scattered in a way that naturally outlines a spectacular wonder, a unique romantic landscape exclusive to Qiandao Lake. The autumn artistic vibe in the mountains is in full swing. Check in at the exclusive art wall, collect limited-edition autumn stamps, and receive exquisite landscape bookmarks, light-and-shadow postcards, and Qiandao Lake planter cups, turning the autumn scenery of Qiandao Lake into a unique memory you can take home. # Pestana Palace

Belém, Lisbon, Portugal

![Image 1](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Pestana-2.jpg)![Image 2](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Pestana-5.jpg)![Image 3](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Pestana-4.jpg)![Image 4](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Pestana-3.jpg)![Image 5](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/wp-content/uploads/2017/04/Pestana-1.jpg)

## why we love it

Once the estate of a cocoa baron, the Pestana Palace has been converted into a hotel and brought back to its former glory, which greets you immediately in the form of an opulent stained glass entryway and the estate's surrounding tropical gardens. Guests get the royal experience here, free to lounge in the indoor and outdoor pools, or dine in the two restaurants that serve Portuguese cuisine with a French twist. While the grounds feel private a secluded, the hotel is near the center of town—it's just seven miles from the Lisbon airport, and close to all the famous monuments of the Belém District.

Originally featured in[The Lisbon Guide](https://goop.com/city-guide/the-lisbon-guide)

# 48 Hours in Istanbul

Written by:[Brianna Peters](https://goop.com/goop-authors/brianna-peters)Published on:September 2, 2026

![Image 1](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/height=75,width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/media/2026/08/27/istanbul.png)

Naming a favorite destination feels like naming a favorite child: impossible, yet, if pressed, you could probably choose. For me, it’s Istanbul. Istanbul has a rare kind of vigor to it that you don't often get to experience twice. I first visited [years ago](https://goop.com/travel/experiences/turkey-guide) (it's where I got engaged), and when I returned three years later, the city somehow eclipsed my memory of it. That’s the magic of Istanbul: it’s unlike anywhere else. Stretching between two continents, it blends European and Asian influences with thousands of years of history, leaving behind remnants, ruins, and traditions from long-since-vanished empires. At the same time, it still has a distinctly modern energy and newness that match its bustling-metropolis reputation. The history alone is reason enough to go, but for me, the delicious food, fantastic shopping, bathhouse culture, and sense of discovery make Istanbul a must-visit.

If you only have a few days to explore, here's how I’d spend them.

## WHERE TO STAY

It's almost impossible to choose where to stay in Istanbul—there are _that_ many fantastic hotels. The [Peninsula Istanbul](https://goop.com/place/peninsula-hotel-in-istanbul) in Karakoy is a waterfront spot by the Golden Horn, right in the action and well-positioned for exploring the Asian side of the city. The [Mandarin Oriental](https://www.mandarinoriental.com/en/istanbul/bosphorus) has incredible Bosphorus views, an enchanting garden spa, and lively energy.

[The Raffles Istanbul](https://www.raffles.com/istanbul/) is the place to be if you're a creature of (many) comforts—there's don't-have-to-lift-a-finger 24-hour butler service, fantastic in-room soaking tubs, incredible shopping (it's near the uber popular Zorlu shopping center, where local department store Beymen's has cool Turkish brands), and sweeping views of all of the city. It also has one of the most stunning subterranean spas—complete with a whirlpool tub, sauna, and steam—that’s perfect for a morning hydrotherapy circuit.

If you're a history buff, stay at the [Ciragan Palace Kempinski](https://www.kempinski.com/en/ciragan-palace). Before it was a hotel, it was a sultan's imperial palace, and the pure opulence of the interiors and lush outdoor gardens are proof.It’s also home to the [Sanitas Spa](https://www.kempinski.com/en/ciragan-palace/luxury-spa-in-istanbul/massages-spa-treatments/sultan-treatment), a beautiful, intimate spa that offers a particularly special take on the traditional Turkish hammam experience.

And on that note: If you’re ever going to indulge in a hotel spa treatment, this is the place to do it. It’s not just that it’s fantastically exfoliating and will leave your skin softer than a baby’s; it’s also that a true Turkish bath is methodical, precise, and rigorous—and unlike any other spa treatment I've tried. Carve out time to truly experience the ritual (more on that below), but for shaking the plane off's sake, have a spa treatment booked at your hotel for the night you arrive. Think of it as a hammam _lite_.

![Image 2](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/media/2026/08/28/hotels.png)

The Mandarin Oriental; The Raffles Istanbul; Ciragan Palace Kempinski

## WHAT TO DO

## Day One

Start your morning early with a traditional Turkish breakfast. Raffles has a truly fantastic one with staples like menemen (scrambled eggs cooked with green peppers, olive oil, and tomatoes), sucuk (a type of Turkish sausage), and simit (a toasted, bagel-adjacent bread with honey and whipped cheese). I like to hit the ground running with sightseeing so I can chill later in the day when my energy starts to wane. Old Town is home to many of the city’s historic palaces, mosques, and monuments. There is a _lot_ to see, so if you, like me, get easily overwhelmed by hours-long history tours, try splitting up the excursions.

Note: For visits to mosques and religious sites, women are required to cover their shoulders, knees, and hair, so dress accordingly and pack a pashmina, [scarf](https://goop.com/gwyn-brigid-silk-scarf/p), or [wrap](https://www.whiteandwarren.com/collections/cashmere-travel-wrap-for-women/products/cashmere-travel-wrap-sangria) that’s easy to take on and off.

[Topkapi Palace](https://muze.gen.tr/muze-detay/topkapi) is a highlight—and my favorite palace. It was home to all the Ottoman sultans for four centuries (until 1839), and it's incredible how well-preserved it is given the sheer size of the property. There are dedicated sections for religious relics and clothing, but the real draw is the jewels and gems, including the famous 86-carat Spoonmaker Diamond. You'll want to spend at least two to three hours here, and I highly recommend getting the add-on tickets to explore the Harem. Fun fact: Legend has it that the fountain in the Imperial Council Chamber was used to prevent outsiders from eavesdropping on viziers discussing secrets and state business.

![Image 3](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/media/2026/08/27/breakfast.png)

Breakfast at The Raffles Istanbul; University of Istanbul square near the Grand Bazaar

For lunch, take the tram (it's easy to navigate) to the Spice Bazaar and pop into traditional Turkish restaurant [Pandeli](https://www.pandeli.com.tr/) for some meze and a tea break. You can't go wrong with the döner kebab, lamb, or topik.

After lunch, head over to the Hagia Sophia. An architectural marvel, it has been transformed from a Byzantine Christian church to an Ottoman mosque to a museum, then back to a mosque over the years. It’s an active mosque, so visitors can't go downstairs, but you can still tour upstairs. Many frescoes and mosaics have been destroyed or covered over time, but you can still see some.

Just a few steps away is the [Basilica Cistern](http://yerebatansarnici.com/), the largest ancient cistern beneath the city of Istanbul. It's fascinating to see how water was filtered in the Byzantine era and to check out the popular Medusa columns—there's an array of mismatched Doric, Corinthian, and Ionic pillars, recycled from the ruins of other structures. If you have time, line up to go inside the Blue Mosque. A UNESCO World Heritage site, it has grand domes and thousands of blue-painted Iznik tiles inside.

![Image 4](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/media/2026/08/28/basilica%20and%20dama.png)

Basilica Cistern; DAMA

The Hippodrome of Constantinople (now called Sultanahmet Square) is a nearby city square that was once the city’s arena for social gatherings and sporting events. It's worth a quick walk and wander (it’s where the Horses of Saint Mark originally resided before they were looted during the Fourth Crusade and taken to Venice).

While you’re in the Old City, grab a pre-dinner drink and meze at [Lokanta 1741](https://lokanta1741.com/)—it has an incredible rooftop that's super romantic. Or head straight to Nisantasi, a chic neighborhood with tons of good shopping (check out Vakko for cotton pieces and Gizia for Turkish brands) and places to eat and drink. [Lips Wine Bar](https://www.instagram.com/lipswinebar/?hl=en) is fantastic for small plates and a glass (or two) of wine. For outdoor seating and people watching, try [Foxy Nisantasi](https://followthefoxy.com/). If you want something more substantial, try the gastropub [DAMA](https://www.instagram.com/dama.ist/?hl=en) Nisantasi. It's more casual and lively—but the food, especially the mideye dolma, is delicious.

## Day Two

I'm not saying you should book a trip to Istanbul solely around visiting [Zeyrek Çinili Hamam](https://www.zeyrekcinilihamam.com/en)—but I'm not _not_ saying it. This is the kind of treatment that’s so good you hope your flight gets canceled so that you can stay and book it again. Ask for Kübra—she was the most thoughtful, warm, overall fantastic spa attendant who took me through the whole experience.

Tucked between ancient cisterns and mosques, it's a traditional Turkish hammam that's over 500 years old. Recently renovated (it took over 13 years to complete), the experience starts the second you set foot inside. As you head into the hammam, the relaxation begins. You sit and repeatedly pour hot and cold water over your body before your hammam guide begins vigorously scrubbing every inch of you down with a textured kese glove. It's followed by a hydrating, yet detoxifying mud body mask. Afterward, you rinse off and walk over to a large marble slab in the center of the room. Stretched out on steam-warmed marble, you're draped in a whipped meringue foam cloud of soap bubbles as you're firmly, yet rhythmically massaged. Once you're finished, you float out of the hammam and get to relax even further on cushy daybeds with some tea and treats. Even if your hammam treatment only lasts an hour or two, build in extra time to visit the on-site museum and art gallery. The museum has artifacts from the restoration and delves into the deep history of hammam culture.

![Image 5](https://goop-img.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=100,fit=crop,gravity=0.5x0.5,quality=95,format=auto,onerror=redirect,metadata=copyright/media/2026/08/28/Zeyrek%20C%CC%A7inili%20Hamam.png)

Zeyrek Çinili Hamam

The At-Home Bathhouse Ritual

I still think about my treatment at Sanitas Spa, which starts with 20 minutes in the sauna to loosen your muscles before your spa attendant ushers you into the marble hammam. The ritual includes steaming, exfoliation, and a full-body soap massage, finishing with a body mask made of honey, milk, and rosewater. While the mask warms up and works its magic, you get a heavenly scalp massage, shampoo, and conditioning treatment. Once everything is washed away, you cozy up in a fluffy towel while your attendant spritzes your skin with rosewater tonic. Rose has deep roots in Turkish beauty rituals, dating back to the Ottoman Empire, and Turkey remains one of the world’s leading producers of rose oil.

Now, once a week, I try to untether myself from the busyness of 21st-century American life and make time to recreate the ritual. After using a sauna blanket, I steam up my shower, vigorously exfoliate with a body scrub, and lather up with mountains of silky soap bubbles using a rose-scented body wash. When I get out, I finish by massaging in body oil from head to toe.

Around the corner from the hammam is the Aqueduct of Valens, an ancient aqueduct built in the 4th century. Then head to the Grand Bazaar for some shopping. On the way, stop by Aynen Dürüm, a super low-key, no-frills kebab shack that serves the most delicious and tender lamb dürüm (wraps). The Grand Bazaar can be overwhelming at first (there are over 4,000 shops), but if you skip the counterfeit designer bags and tchotchkes and head straight to the “Old Bazaar,” you can find cool antique trinkets, jewelry, caftans, towels, soaps, teas, and more.

In the early evening, walk across the historic Galata Bridge before arriving at Galataport, a long waterfront strip of shops and restaurants. Check out [Communité Galataport](https://www.instagram.com/communitestore/?hl=en) for some more shopping (I especially love the local Turkish brands like Pelcare). A late-afternoon cruise on the Bosphorus is the best way to see both the Asian and European sides of the city—sit back, relax, and enjoy the honey golden sunset over the city.

When you get off, head to [Aheste](https://ahesterestaurant.com/) for dinner. The intimate Turkish bistro is right in the Pera neighborhood, and one place I'll always make time to visit when I'm in Istanbul. The tasting menu is absolutely worth it—you get five delicious courses (think dudi Persian rice with crispy onion and tuna kadayif with pomegranate sour mayo), and they'll kindly swap out a course for dietary preferences or restrictions. For drinks, I got the Sor—a delicious magenta thyme-and-hibiscus-infused gin cocktail with a fluffy vanilla-egg-white foam. Afterward, if you’re still up for it, pop over to [Comedus](https://comedus.com.tr/) wine bar and split a bottle of Turkish rosé.
